Out-of-graph OS packages are excluded when mixed with in-graph packages in SBOM
## Description

When scanning SBOM files with Trivy, many OS packages are missing from the output. This issue occurs when both in-graph OS packages (packages directly connected to the OS component in the dependency graph) and out-of-graph OS packages (orphaned packages not connected to the OS component) are present in the SBOM. Currently, only in-graph packages are included in the final output, while out-of-graph packages are excluded.

This is a general issue that affects all operating systems and SBOM formats.

## Environment

- Trivy version: Latest main branch
- SBOM formats: CycloneDX, SPDX (potentially affects both)
- Test case: Amazon Linux 2023 (but affects all OS types)

## Reproduction Steps

1. Use the SBOM file from the discussion
2. Run: `trivy sbom --list-all-pkgs --format json 9006.json`
3. Count packages: `jq '.Results[0].Packages | length'`

## Expected Behavior

Based on the original SBOM components:
```bash
jq '[.components[] | select(.type == "library")] | length' 9006.json
# Returns: 194
```

Both in-graph and out-of-graph OS packages should be included in the final output.

## Actual Behavior

Current Trivy output:
```bash
./trivy sbom --list-all-pkgs --format json 9006.json | jq '.Results[0].Packages | length'
# Returns: 27
```

Only in-graph OS packages are included, while out-of-graph packages are excluded.

## Root Cause

The issue occurs in the `addOrphanPkgs` function in `pkg/sbom/io/decode.go`. When both in-graph and out-of-graph OS packages exist:
1. In-graph packages are processed first and added to a PackageInfo entry
2. Out-of-graph packages are processed separately and put in a new PackageInfo entry instead of being merged with existing ones
3. Only the first PackageInfo entry is retained in the final output

## Impact

- Missing OS packages means vulnerability scanning may miss security issues in those packages
- Affects all OS types (Alpine, Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, etc.) when scanning SBOM files
- Potentially affects both CycloneDX and SPDX formats
- Reduces accuracy of security scanning results

## Related Discussion

This issue is based on the discussion: https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/discussions/9006

If you would like to use the AWS ECR Public Gallery, there is a separate API and IAM permission associated with it that needs to be used.

The AWS CLI command is as follows for logging in to such a registry:

Note the use of `ecr-public` vs `ecr`, and the region I believe has to be `us-east-1` (global).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The ability to manage AWS ECR Public authorization tokens via `external-secrets`. This would greatly simplify credential management for OCI repositories which are hosted in the AWS public gallery. Right now its a mess of cronjobs to try and fudge it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
One solution might be the implementation of an `ECRPublicAuthorizationToken` kind. I don't really know enough about the implementation to know whether or not adding a `scope: <private|public>` to the `spec` might be possible while still using an `ECRAuthorizationToken`.

**Additional context**
The `ecrpublic` service appears to have dedicated support in the AWS SDK for it:

https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/tree/main/service/ecrpublic

I would have a go at trying to implement something, but fear the result would be somewhat crude.

Support specifying swift Generic Type Constraints
Consider the following struct:

```
#[typeshare]
#[derive(Serialize, Debug)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct AccountPayload<A> {
    pub id: String,
    pub payload: A
}
```

It is generated as: (we have Sendable in the typeshare.toml file)
```
public struct AccountPayload<A: Codable>: Codable, Sendable {
	public let id: String
	public let payload: A
…
	}
}
```

However, generic type `A` (and others) may also have another type constraint (in this case `Sendable` supplied) so that it needs to be generated as:
```
public struct CoreAccountMenuEntry<A: Codable & Sendable>: Codable, Sendable {
…
```

### Suggestion:

An additional decorator parameter in the toml:
`default_generic_decorators = ["Sendable"]`

And/or in the rust definitions itself:
`[typeshare(swift="Whatever", swift_generic="A:Sendable & AnotherProtocol,B:Sendable & SomeOtherProtocol")]` where A and B are generics specified in the struct. (I added B here in case there is more than one generic)

Rate limiting is not updated until after the handler returns
### Description
A long-running plugin callable with a rate limit can be called again in the same rate-limit context while it is still running. Metrics are not updated [until after a Rule's handler completes](https://github.com/sopel-irc/sopel/blob/36b7c2f1064e7d734e50a66b24270cf7c8949426/sopel/plugins/rules.py#L1071-L1085), because the current metrics also need its exit code, but [rate limiting is checked before dispatching the callable](https://github.com/sopel-irc/sopel/blob/36b7c2f1064e7d734e50a66b24270cf7c8949426/sopel/bot.py#L584-L624).

### Reproduction steps
1. Build a long-running plugin callable ("dummy" way: `time.sleep(10)`)
2. Give the callable a command, let's say `.ratefail`
3. Apply `@plugin.rate(60)` or whatever test value you like
4. Try to call `.ratefail` twice from a non-admin user (admins bypass rate limits)
5. Actual result: `.ratefail` will run twice

### Expected behavior
`.ratefail` cannot be called twice because it is rate limited.

### Environment
- Sopel `.version`: 7, 8-dev, probably earlier
- Sopel installed via: any method
- Python version: any supported
- Operating system: any supported

We discussed this on IRC today, and @Exirel already has a plan of attack. Therefore I've assigned the issue to him—but since we already thought there was an open issue about this when there actually wasn't, I thought it was a good idea to make one.

I need to add a new converter called `@get` to be used to simply call `settings.get` with specified key and use whatever value is there with the current type.

Example:

```python

Tenant package relies on mutable global state
The `tenant` package is used for (among other things) extracting a tenant ID from a `context.Context`. 

There are two separate implementations of this logic:
* Logic that understands tenant IDs separated by a `|` and so can return multiple tenant IDs from a context.
* Logic that does not understand tenant IDs separate by a `|` and so returns an error in this case.

There is a `WithDefaultResolver` that changes which logic is used, [via mutating a global](https://github.com/grafana/dskit/blob/4cfd2dc0d14c7e79e6482f231c8c58ae6ceea6d7/tenant/resolver.go#L14-L17). [Mimir](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/blob/e974d3d816e42b8c182b7acbc0e205ce5251da44/pkg/mimir/mimir.go#L720-L727) and [Loki](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/bd505f8e2d37172ff35a89f4ac42efec9566a263/pkg/loki/modules.go#L332-L337) do this in response to some form of multi-tenant queries being enabled or disabled by configuration.

This is a problem because the behavior of huge portions of each database can change by changes made far away from the code in question. It also makes it more difficult to unit test the code in question since adjusting the global state for a single test affects the behavior of every other test.

I propose:

* Remove the `WithDefaultResolver` to prevent mutation of global state
* Remove all global state since it's unnecessary. The logic of `MultiResolver` would move to the global `tenant.TenantID()` and `tenant.TenantIDs()` methods. 
* This would also make `SingleResolver`, `MultiResolver`, and `Resolver` unnecessary

This would require changes in Mimir and Loki to reject multi-tenant queries when they aren't enabled. However, this would result in a better design anyway since the databases are checking for and enforcing exactly what they intend to enforce.

Bug: CronController performs back-scheduling when re-enabling JobConfig
The CronController will perform back-scheduling based on the `status.lastScheduleTime` and `spec.schedule.constraints.notBefore`. We will always `notBefore` to the current time if we detect that the schedule is updated, to avoid wrongly back-scheduling when the user shortens the cron schedule (e.g. every 00:00 changed to start of every hour, do not schedule until start of next hour).

However, the case when we update `spec.schedule.disabled` from `true` to `false` is not handled, causing it to still back-schedule incorrectly.

Restrict library versions to be visible only when using specific compilers
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm setting up a local compiler explorer instance for my company. We have several product versions, each of which ships with a compiler capable of targetting several architectures, and each of those architectures has their own set of static libraries available to them.

I am trying to create a workflow where a user can select compilers targetting different architectures from the compiler dropdown menu, and depending on which architecture their compiler is specified as targetting, different static library paths will be chosen for libraries they choose to add. My rationale for this is that it would be helpful to have an accurate representation of what the generated code looks like when compiling with the "Compile to Binary" option enabled, without making the user have to select their target architecture more than once.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
In a perfect world I'd like to have a configuration option exposed to limit the libraries available for a given compiler to a subset of the libraries defined under `libs`.

For instance, if a library `widget` existed with library versions `trunk-x86_64` and `trunk-aarch64` defined, a compiler `gcc_x86_64` could be restricted to only have the x86_64 version of the library visible through `compiler.gcc_x86_64.libs=widget.trunk-x86_64`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Issue #1590 mentions that "we already [have] libraries per compiler", and it seems like some mechanism is in place to allow external compiler explorer instances to integrate their own compilers with unique library versions together (as seems to be the case with godbolt.ms from godbolt.org), but using a model like that in this case seems like it would lead to a full compiler explorer instance running per product version, per architecture, which in our case could mean hundreds of servers running. That seems very inefficient way to filter a list of file path strings. I admit that I haven't been able to figure out how that integration works yet by looking at the code, so I might be missing some straightforward solution to this.

One solution that comes to mind is making library versions for all architectures visible in the library version selection list, and relying on the user to choose the right library for their architecture of choice. This seems error-prone, since for every library a user might want to include, they would have to select the right choice from a (potentially quite long) list of similar-looking architectures, and possibly silently causing the wrong behaviour if they choose the wrong one.

Another solution I've considered is bumping up the level of abstraction, giving each product version its own compiler explorer instance and making each language in the instance qualified by the architecture its compilers will be targetting, which would allow the desired behaviour to exist (since libraries can be defined per-language). it might work t, but it doesn't seem like a good idea, since it's using compiler explorer features in ways that aren't really related to how they're supposed to work, and in this case it would make the compiler selection dropdown basically useless since there would only ever be one item available.

**Additional context**
If anyone has any suggestions about existing ways to solve this problem, I'm more than happy to hear them. I might be totally missing something in the CE codebase that supports this use case!

Clear up RuntimeConfig
As a result of https://github.com/solid/community-server/issues/67, `RuntimeConfig` was implemented in https://github.com/solid/community-server/pull/71. While a good interim solution, it creates some annoyances that we should strive to fix.

For instance, `SimpleResourceStore` now gets a `RuntimeConfig` argument. That is quite messy, because now `SimpleResourceStore` needs to know (and depends on) which arguments are passed as config files and which are passed via CLI, which is none of its concern.

What I think we should be doing instead, is pass command-line arguments to the configuration JSON _before_ things get instantiated. Does Components.js somehow allow the definition of constants, which are passed around? If so, the CLI could write such a constants file, which then includes the others.

I guess I simply don't understand (from #67)

> we depend on values from the CLI, which are only available after component instantiation.

It seems to me that `base`, `port`, `rootFilepath` can all be read from the CLI before we instantiate components?

No matter how we solve it, it seems to be that:
- `SimpleResourceStore` should not know about CLI or config params
- Hence, `SimpleResourceStore` should only be instantiated after CLI params have been propagated/merged with config

Add functions thats subtracts a field from another field
See openaddresses/openaddresses#2195

Here's a example data that's motivating this: 

```
{
  "addrnum": "400 E",
  "unitid": "E",
  "fulladdr": "400 E EMERY AVE"
}
```

In this case it's very difficult if not impossible to write a `regexp` function that would know the difference between a unit `E` and an `E` that's an address pre-directional.   That is, without awareness of other fields values, it's not possible to know if the street value shoud be `E EMERY AVE` or `EMERY AVE`.  The data motivating this also has a wide variety of unit formats:

* `[0-9]+`
* `[A-Z]`
* `[A-Z]-?[0-9]+`
* `[0-9]+[A-Z]`
* `BLDG [0-9]+`
* a variety of one-off values that can't be captured by regexes easily

These conform function would look something like:

```
{
  "number": {
    "function": "remove_postfix",
    "field": "addrnum",
    "field_to_remove": "unitid",
  },
  "street": {
    "function": "remove_prefix",
    "field": "fulladdr",
    "field_to_remove": "addrnum"    
  },
  "unit": "unitid"
}
```

The result of these functions would be:

```
{
  "number": "400",
  "street": "EMERY AVE",
  "unit": "E"
}
```

In a larger context, there are some sources that have `number` identified as a distinct field but the `street` value can only be derived using a `regexp`.  In these cases, the `regexp` function can be replaced with `remove_prefix`.

Infinite loop in repeatedPageValues.ReadValues
Run this test to reproduce:
```
func TestLoop(t *testing.T) {
	type testType struct {
		ListOfLists [][]int
	}
	instance := testType{ListOfLists: [][]int{{1, 3, 5}, nil, {2, 4, 6}}}
	buf := parquet.NewGenericBuffer[testType]()
	_, err := buf.Write([]testType{instance})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	rg := parquet.RowGroup(buf)
	chunks := rg.ColumnChunks()
	require.Equal(t, 1, len(chunks))
	pages := chunks[0].Pages()
	p, err := pages.ReadPage()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	vals := make([]parquet.Value, p.NumValues())
	_, _ = p.Values().ReadValues(vals)
}
```

It looks like the infinite loop is caused because this check always evaluates to false:
https://github.com/segmentio/parquet-go/blob/b03c0471ebb0eadd7fc54f41fccd58dafca80eee/page_values.go#L39

As soon as the `nil` is removed from the `testType` instantiation, the test completes successfully.

**What happened**:
The orphan controller always used to ignore machines that are being just in creation. I.e that `status.CurrentStatus.Phase` was not set. However, with the introduction of `CrashLoopBackOff`, and when the first try for machine creation fails and any further retries lead to the possibility of VMs showing up on the consoled prior to updating the machine object and hence is treated as an orphan VM. This is causing this race to lead to this state.
Refer - [machine safety code](https://github.com/gardener/machine-controller-manager/blob/master/pkg/controller/machine_safety.go#L575-L580)

**What you expected to happen**:
For the VM to be not treated as an orphan and allow it to join.  

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Try creating a VM that should return an error on the first creation and post which the next creations should lead to this race condition on providers that return after too long. 

**Anything else we need to know**:

One way I think of fixing this would be to ignore machines in crashLoopBackoff while trying to clean up orphan machines.

Time duration for `handshake_first` option is not respected for leafnodes
### Observed behavior

According to this [ADR](https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-40.md) passing a time duration for the `handshake_first` option, makes the server backward compatible because after the timeout the server is supposed to use the standard TLS flow.

This works for standard connections (from clients) but not for leafnodes.
If the leafnode doesn't declare the `handshake_first` field in the `remotes` section, its connection will be never accepted by the server

I'm able to connect to my server using `nats-cli` with or without the `--tlsfirst` flag (because of the timeout) but the leafnode can connect to the server only if it use the field in the remote section.

### Expected behavior

A leafnode connection without `handshake_first` is accepted (standard TLS flow) after the initial timeout

### Server and client version

nats-server: v2.10.18 (both server and leafnode)
nats-cli: 0.1.5

### Host environment

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

Main server has this configuration
```
TLS = {
  cert_file: $CERT_FILE
  key_file: $KEY_FILE
  ca_file: $CA_FILE
  verify_and_map: true
  timeout: 2
  handshake_first: 500ms
}

tls : $TLS

leafnodes {
    port: 20023
    tls: $TLS
}
```

The leafnode has this one
```

  cert_file: $CERT_FILE
  key_file: $KEY_FILE
  ca_file: $CA_FILE
  verify_and_map: true
  handshake_first: 500ms

tls : $TLS

leafnodes {
  remotes: [
    {
      url: $SERVER
      tls {
         cert_file: $CERT_FILE
         key_file: $KEY_FILE
         ca_file: $CA_FILE
         handshake_first: true
      }
      account: $MY_ACCOUNT
    }
  ] 
}
```

In this case works, but if I remove the `handshake_first` from `remotes` section it doesn't

```
TLS = {
  cert_file: $CERT_FILE
  key_file: $KEY_FILE
  ca_file: $CA_FILE
  verify_and_map: true
  handshake_first: 500ms
}

tls : $TLS

leafnodes {
  remotes: [
    {
      url: $SERVER
      tls {

      }

Custom serialization for stores
<!--
Please fill out this entire template so that we can evaluate your proposal as quickly as possible.
-->

## Proposal

Currently we can only disable serialization of store's value via `serialize: 'ignore'` setting, but sometimes we do want to transfer state from server to the client, even if this state is represented in non-json shape - e.g. `Date` or `Map`

Idea is to add custom serialization config to stores:

```ts
const $map = createStore(new Map<number, number>(), {
      serialize: {
        write: map => [...map.entries()],
        read: jsonMap => new Map(jsonMap),
      },
})
```

Which would allow to introduce custom serialization to SSR usecases:
1. We have a store with non-serializable value - e.g. Map
```ts
    const $map = createStore(new Map<number, number>(), {
      serialize: {
        write: map => [...map.entries()],
        read: jsonMap => new Map(jsonMap),
      },
    })
```

2. During SSR we are creating separate `Scope` for each request, as usual, then run the logic
```ts
const scope = fork()

await allSettled(appStarted, {scope, params: req })
```

3. After logic is settled, we need to extract stores data to stringify it to JSON to transfer to client.
At this moment `serialize.write` method of `$map` will be called

```ts
const serverValues = serialize(scope)

serverValues[$map.sid] // has number[][], which is json-representation of Map<number, number>

const jsonString = JSON.stringify(serverValues) // no errors, which would happen because of Map
```

4. At the client we want to create a client scope and fill it with values from the server.
At this moment `serialize.read` method of `$map` is called

```ts
const clientScope = fork({
 values: serverValues
})

clientScope.getState($map) // Map<number, number> with values from the server

```

**Caveats**
We have two ways to setup `values` in `fork` call:
- `Map<Store, Value> | [Store, Value][]`, which is used for tests and sometimes as a di-mechanism
- `Record<string, Value>`, which is used for server-calculated values in the shape of json
We need a way to decide, when we need to call `serialize.read` methods and when we don't need it

I think, in the first case we have a clear user intent to set a specific value to specific store:
```ts
const scope = fork({
 values: [
    [$map, new Map(...)]
 ]
})
```
so here we don't need to deal with serialization at all.

The second case is not considered a public api for manual values setup - only to provide json with server values:
```ts
fork({
  values: {
    "-dsg4gf": [[0, 1], [2, 3]]
  }
})
```
so here we clearly need to use `serialize.read`

Jobs stopping unexpectedly
Supersedes the following issues:
- #805
- #514
- #232
- #231

## Bug description

Under certain conditions, cron jobs stop executing unexpectedly without any error or log output. This behavior has been observed in jobs running at high frequency (e.g., every second or every few seconds) as well as jobs scheduled less frequently. The job ceases operation after a variable period (from as little as 15 minutes to several days) and does not resume until the application or container is restarted. In some cases, the issue appears to coincide with low available machine resources or system time adjustments, while in others it occurs without any apparent external trigger.

## Root cause analysis


The root cause of these issues is the way the library calculates the time until the next scheduled execution. The process involves two separate fetches of the current time within the `sendAt` function, leading to a potential race condition:

### 1. Initial time fetch

When `sendAt` starts, it fetches the current time to calculate the next execution time based on the cron expression <sup>([source](https://github.com/kelektiv/node-cron/blob/8e509f3ad7dcd5d250e75a41417830b9b01c2bdb/src/time.ts#L87C2-L91))</sup>.

```ts
sendAt(i?: number): DateTime | DateTime[] {
  let date =
    this.realDate && this.source instanceof DateTime
      ? this.source
      : DateTime.local();
```

### 2. Timeout calculation

After `sendAt` completes, the library fetches the current time again to compute the remaining delay <sup>([source](https://github.com/kelektiv/node-cron/blob/8e509f3ad7dcd5d250e75a41417830b9b01c2bdb/src/time.ts#L140-L142))</sup>.

```ts
getTimeout() {
  return Math.max(-1, this.sendAt().toMillis() - DateTime.local().toMillis());
}
```

If the delay between these two time fetches is sufficiently large (due to execution delays or a system time change), the computed timeout can become negative. In such cases, the job is stopped immediately <sup>([source](https://github.com/kelektiv/node-cron/blob/8e509f3ad7dcd5d250e75a41417830b9b01c2bdb/src/job.ts#L309-L322))</sup>.

```ts
if (timeout >= 0) {
  // ...
  setCronTimeout(timeout);
} else {
  this.stop();
}
```

## Reproduction

The bug can be reproduced by stubbing `Date.now()` to simulate either a prolonged execution of `sendAt` or a system time jump between the initial time fetch and the subsequent calculation. This controlled manipulation forces `getTimeout` to compute a negative timeout, which triggers the job to stop.

See the [implemented test case](https://github.com/kelektiv/node-cron/pull/963/commits/7a81971abd0b431f23c4816c5a4971831f94aa09#diff-29a4a49c4a4e84d0dd0917be4f7921905d0122a2bafa1d9d2749557359de4bb7R22-R45).

## Proposed fix

Introduce a configurable threshold with sensible default to distinguish between minor delays and significant timing discrepancies. When a negative timeout is detected, if the negative timeout is:

- **Within threshold:** schedule the job immediately (and log a warning)
- **Outside threshold:** skip the current execution (and log a warning)

This solution combines the strengths of either always executing immediately or always skipping execution while mitigating their drawbacks:

- **Balanced execution:** in real-world scenarios, minor delays (for example, those under 500ms/1000ms) are often acceptable. Executing the job immediately in these cases prevents unnecessary stoppages and keeps high-frequency tasks running with minimal interruption.

- **Flexibility:** making the threshold configurable allows developers to tailor the behavior based on the criticality and frequency of their cron jobs.

- **Observability:** logging warnings when a large negative timeout is encountered provides critical insight into timing issues. This transparency aids in diagnostics and helps developers fine-tune the threshold settings based on observed behavior in production.

### Feature description

**Feature Request**: Extend io.kestra.core.tasks.executions.counts to Monitor by Namespaces

**Background:**
The current implementation of the io.kestra.core.tasks.executions.counts task provides execution counts for a list of flows. This can be used to send alerts if specific conditions about execution counts are met. While monitoring based on specific flow names is useful, there are use cases where one might want to monitor execution counts across an entire namespace.

**Feature:**
Extend the io.kestra.core.tasks.executions.counts task to accept a list of Namespaces as input, in addition to the existing Flows. If a namespace is provided, the task should monitor the counts for all the flows within that namespace.

**Input Parameters:**
Flows (Existing): A list of flow IDs to monitor.
Namespaces (New): A list of namespaces to monitor. If a namespace is provided, all the flows within that namespace should be monitored.

**Output:**
The output should remain consistent with the current format, detailing the flows that met the specified condition. If the flows from a namespace meet the condition, those specific flow details should be included in the output.

By allowing monitoring based on namespaces, users can keep a more holistic check on execution counts, especially useful when managing a large number of flows grouped under a specific namespace. This ensures better observability and quicker response times in case of anomalies.

io.kestra.core.tasks.executions.counts:

    - a.b.c

random states may have same seed
The current implementation of seeding the random number generator is:

```
seeds = [self._numpy_state.randint(np.iinfo(np.int32).max) for i in sizes]
```

This can result in repetition of seeds => random sequences are the same, which is probably not what users intend. The reasoning is the same as the [birthday problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birthday_problem) in probability.

```
from __future__ import division

import numpy as np
from scipy.misc import comb, factorial


def prob_same(k, n=np.iinfo(np.int32).max):
    '''
    Compute the probability that at least two seeds are the same
    '''
    different = comb(n, k, exact=True) * factorial(k, exact=True)
    total = n ** k
    prob_all_different = different / total
    return 1 - prob_all_different
```

Here's a few figures:
```
In [246]: prob_same(1000)
Out[246]: 0.00023257080042193845

In [247]: prob_same(10000)
Out[247]: 0.023011865852016755

In [248]: prob_same(50000)
Out[248]: 0.4412591367423576
```

So if there are 50000 chunks, there's a 44% chance that a seed will be repeated. Probably no big deal for most use cases, but it would be better to not have to make this assumption.

It's possible to eliminate this by just sampling with replacement. Ie. change the implementation to something like:
```
seeds = self._numpy_state.choice(np.iinfo(np.int32).max, size=len(sizes), replace=True)
```

I don't know if this alternative implementation would be totally valid, since it seems like more may be required. See this [paper by L'Ecuyer](http://www.iro.umontreal.ca/~lecuyer/myftp/papers/wsc15rng.pdf). But it would effectively guarantee different seeds.

Optimize internal calls to UnmarshalCBOR() for ByteString, RawTag, and SimpleValue
## Problem

Currently, the unreleased changes in PR #636 and #645 cause the input data to be checked twice when `UnmarshalCBOR()` is called internally.

`UnmarshalCBOR()` checks input data because it can be called by user apps providing bad data.  However, the codec already checks input data before internally calling `UnmarshalCBOR()` so the 2nd check is redundant.

## Solution

Optimize by making the codec no longer directly call `UnmarshalCBOR()` if the private `unmarshalCBOR()` is implemented by the type:
- Internally, the codec will call the private `unmarshalCBOR()` to avoid validating data twice.
- `MarshalCBOR()` will be a simple wrapper that checks data for validity before calling the private `unmarshalCBOR()`.

## Status

This optimization is being tested locally.  It will be merged and fuzzed for longer durations before release v2.7.1 and v2.8.0.

A merge statement with the output clause could look like this:
```sql

MERGE dso.products AS t
USING dsi.products AS s
	ON s.ProductID = t.ProductID
WHEN MATCHED 
	AND NOT (t.[ProductName] = s.[ProductName] OR (ISNULL(t.[ProductName], s.[ProductName]) IS NULL))
THEN
	UPDATE SET t.[ProductName] = s.[ProductName]

WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET THEN
INSERT ([ProductID]
           ,[ProductName])
     VALUES
           (s.[ProductID]
           ,s.[ProductName])

WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE  THEN
	DELETE

OUTPUT $action, deleted.* INTO dsi.temp_products;
```

Incorrect re-definition of global variables
The global variable are not correctly handeled in the `__main__` module as they do not remain global.


### Script
```python
from cloudpickle import dumps, loads


VARIABLE = "uninitialized"


def func1():
    global VARIABLE
    print("[func1] global var id{}: {}".format(id(VARIABLE), VARIABLE))
    VARIABLE = "initialized"
    return VARIABLE


# Dump and reload the function
reloaded_f1 = loads(dumps(func1))

# The function call does not change the value of the global VARIABLE
assert reloaded_f1() == "initialized"
print(VARIABLE)

# Changing the value of VARIABLE does not affect the function
VARIABLE = 'test'
assert reloaded_f1() == "initialized"

# But redumping it changes the value
assert loads(dumps(func1))() == "initialized"
print(VARIABLE)
```

### Output
```bash
[func1] global var id140197480377584: uninitialized
uninitialized
[func1] global var id140197483839984: initialized
[func1] global var id140197480295592: test
test
```

I think a way to avoid this is to pass the global variable to `_fill_function` and use `globals()`:
- If the global variable is already present in `globals`, do not do anything.
- If it is not present, add it with the given value.

v1 sender should limit response size
BIP 78 does not restrict the size of the response, but specifies that content length must be included.

The v1 receiver enforces a reasonable limit on the request:

https://github.com/payjoin/rust-payjoin/blob/34ee78d44e1527210a343f4e08128e41a82a67a1/payjoin/src/receive/v1.rs#L95-L97

however, a similar limit was not included in payjoin-cli, `response.bytes().to_vec()` could potentially make unbounded allocations given a large enough response body:

https://github.com/payjoin/rust-payjoin/blob/34ee78d44e1527210a343f4e08128e41a82a67a1/payjoin/src/send/v1.rs#L276-L277

(note that the error mapping also seems inaccurate, not sure what happens in the case of invalid utf8 in the response)

nor is a size limit enforced in the payjoin-cli sender:

https://github.com/payjoin/rust-payjoin/blob/34ee78d44e1527210a343f4e08128e41a82a67a1/payjoin-cli/src/app/v1.rs#L99

because these are unbounded allocations a malicious receiver can cause memory exhaustion for the sender.

there may be other issues in v1, and similarly we should check that the in the v2 implementation no such unbounded allocations (e.g. `r.bytes().to_vec()`) are used for all parties (sender, receiver, directory and relay)

Consider the following markdown:

```
Lorem ipsum.[^a][^b]

[^a]: Foo
[^b]: Bar
```

Which on GitHub, renders thus:

Lorem ipsum.[^a][^b]

[^a]: Foo
[^b]: Bar

With pulldown-cmark **v0.9.6**, these were correctly parsed as two consecutive footnote references:

```

[Feature Request] Process session id
A session id is used to group processes within a session.

For mac/bsd/linix it can be obtained from the [getsid](https://docs.rs/libc/0.2.124/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/libc/fn.getsid.html) system call

For windows it can be found in the [SYSTEM_PROCESS_INFORMATION](https://microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs/doc/windows/Win32/System/WindowsProgramming/struct.SYSTEM_PROCESS_INFORMATION.html) struct from NtQuerySystemInformation which is already being called. Returned character token spans are not correct for some inputs
## Description
For some inputs the character spans returned by `Encoding.getCharTokenSpans()` does not correspond to the correct character span in the input string.

### Expected Behavior
`Encoding.getCharTokenSpans()` should return the correct character span, and it should return the same character spans as when using the same tokenizer in Python.

### Error Message
No error message.

### Steps to reproduce
The error can be reproduced with this short Scala snippet
```
    val someText = "just some string including a £9.00 price"
    val tokenizer = HuggingFaceTokenizer.newInstance("distilbert-base-uncased")
    val encodedText = tokenizer.encode(someText)

    val charSpans = encodedText.getCharTokenSpans()
    val tokens = encodedText.getTokens()
    for (i <- 1 until charSpans.length) {
        println(s"$token: ${tokens(i)}, orig string: ${someText.substring(charSpans(i).getStart, charSpans(i).getEnd)}, span start=${charSpans(i).getStart}, span end=${charSpans(i).getEnd}")
    }
```
This script has the following output
```
token: just, orig string: just, span start=0, span end=4
token: some, orig string: some, span start=5, span end=9
token: string, orig string: string, span start=10, span end=16
token: including, orig string: including, span start=17, span end=26
token: a, orig string: a, span start=27, span end=28
token: £, orig string: £9, span start=29, span end=31
token: ##9, orig string: ., span start=31, span end=32
token: ., orig string: 0, span start=32, span end=33
token: 00, orig string: 0 , span start=33, span end=35
```
So for some reason the 6th token ("£") gets a character span of two characters, and then the rest of the spans are off by one.

Running this very similar Python script
```
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("distilbert-base-uncased")

some_string = "just some string including a £9.00 price"
encoded_input = tokenizer(some_string, return_offsets_mapping=True)

tokens = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(encoded_input["input_ids"])
for token, span in zip(tokens[1:-1], encoded_input["offset_mapping"][1:-1]):
    print(f"token: {token}, orig string: {some_string[span[0]:span[1]]}, span start={span[0]}, span end={span[1]}")
```
gives the following output

token: just, orig string: just, span start=0, span end=4
token: some, orig string: some, span start=5, span end=9
token: string, orig string: string, span start=10, span end=16
token: including, orig string: including, span start=17, span end=26
token: a, orig string: a, span start=27, span end=28
token: £, orig string: £, span start=29, span end=30
token: ##9, orig string: 9, span start=30, span end=31
token: ., orig string: ., span start=31, span end=32
token: 00, orig string: 00, span start=32, span end=34
token: price, orig string: price, span start=35, span end=40
```
And the 6th token ("£") gets a character span of one characters, as expected.

"ai.djl.huggingface:tokenizers:0.19.0"

folder regex matches /^Home/

Change this output of `explain`

folder regex matches /^Home/Family/Us/ =>

The former is unnecessary given that it's an alias to another one-letter flag (I imagine it's there for historical reasons?) and the latter is cumbersome if someone wanted to use the long form (`--unrestricted`). This setup also makes the behavior of the flag ambiguous if new default filters were added in the future. In that case, would I disable all filters with `-uu` or would I need to use `-uuu`?

Given the project's focus on ergonomics and usability, I'd suggest to make `-u` always search all files and to deprecate `-uu`. This would be the equivalent of `ls -a`, giving the user the guarantee that no filters will be applied by default. The main cons of this suggestion is that it's a breaking change and a subtle one: the command would continue to work with `-u` but could return a different set of results.

Feature request: standalone `validate` function for JSON Schema validation
### Use case

To start implementing the new Validation utility, we should implement a `validate` standalone function, which is the core of the Validation utility and is a thin layer around `ajv`, the JSON Schema validation module we're taking a dependency on.

> [!note]
> This issue is open for contributions 🎉 If you're interested in contributing, please leave a comment below so that a maintainer can assign it to you. If you have questions or need clarifications, please don't hesitate to ask. 

### Solution/User Experience

A longer version of this can be found in the unpublished documentation page about the feature, that can be found at `docs/utilities/validation.md`.

The `validate` function should be a synchronous function that takes a single `params` object and acts as an [assertion function](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-3-7.html#assertion-functions) which - as the name suggests - asserts that the event is of a certain type, or throws a `SchemaValidationError` error otherwise.

The `params` object should accept the following items:
- a `payload` - this is the unknown object we want to validate
- a `schema`  - this is the JSON Schema we'll use to validate
- an optional `envelope` parameter of type `string` (more on this later)
- an optional `formats` optional parameter to pass custom formats
- an optional `externalRefs` array of schemas that can be used to supply external references to the main schema
- an optional `ajv` parameter that customers can use to provide their own instance - this is useful when wanting to use a different JSON Schema version/draft

The `validate` function should be generic and accept a type which is the type being asserted, if no type is supplied we'll default to `unknown`.

In terms of implementation, the `validate` function will rely on `ajv` and instantiate its own instance (`new Ajv()`) whenever one is not provided in the `params` object. When creating a new `Ajv` instance, we'll pass down any of the `formats` and `externalRefs` present in the `params` to the `Ajv` constructor.

If instead an `ajv` instance is already supplied, we'll add the `formats` and `externalRefs` using the methods `addFormat()` and `addSchema()`.

Next, the `validate` function should call the `compile()` method on the `ajv` instance using the `schema` provided.

In case an `envelope` is passed, the function will use the `search` function from the `@aws-lambda-powertools/jmespath` module (already installed as dependency) to extract a subset of the `payload` using the `envelope` expression. The resulting object should be the one actually being validated.

Finally, it should validate the data and throw a `SchemaValidationError` error if the validation fails. This is a custom error that should be defined and exported for customers to use. If the validation is successful, the function should return the validated data.

As part of the implementation the implementer should also write unit tests to cover 100% of the files, lines, branches of the code added as part of this issue. All the dependencies needed should already be present in the workspace, ideally the implementation should follow existing project conventions as much as possible.

### Alternative solutions

```

Add `extra_headers` option to HTTP methods in GitHubAPI

**Problem:** Currently, there is no straightforward way to pass custom headers when making requests with the `GitHubAPI` class. This limits the ability to use certain API features or endpoints that require specific headers to be set (such as [these](https://github.com/PyGithub/PyGithub/blob/300c5015d41236eb410b9cbe895258294e3500af/github/Consts.py#L58-L133)).

**Proposed solution:** I propose adding an `extra_headers` parameter to the methods in the `GitHubAPI` class. For example, to fetch stargazers with their corresponding dates:

```python
async def get_stargazers_with_dates(full_repo_name):
    headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3.star+json"}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        gh = gidgethub.httpx.GitHubAPI(client, "basnijholt", oauth_token=token)
        repo_owner, repo_name = full_repo_name.split("/")
        stats_contributors = await gh.getitem(
            f"/repos/{repo_owner}/{repo_name}/stargazers", extra_headers=headers
        )
        return stats_contributors

await get_stargazers_with_dates("basnijholt/adaptive-lighting")
```

Use tuple as function arguments
## 🚀 Feature request

### Current Behavior

If you want to pass a tuple as function arguments you have to deconstruct the tuple, but miss point free syntax.

```typescript
declare const f: (a: A, b: B) => C;

pipe(
  tuple(a, b),
  x => f(...x),
);
```

### Desired Behavior

Use function `apT` to resolve this

```typescript
declare const f: (a: A, b: B) => C;

// apT will apply the tuple as function arguments
const fT: (t: [A, B]) => C = apT(f);

pipe(
  tuple(a, b),
  fT,
);
```

### Suggested Solution

This function could be implemented as

```typescript
const apT: <A extends Array<unknown>, B>(f: (...a: A) => B) => (a: A) => B =
    f => a => f(...a);
```

Bug: Incorrect git config parsing (error when cloning local repository with trailing backslash on Windows)
I ran into a ValueError ("escape character followed by unknown character 102...") when trying to clone a local repository on Windows. The issue turned out to be because of how trailing backslashes interact with how dulwich parses git config files.

**Reproduction steps**

(I think this affects lots of other operations on things that have been cloned from a local remote on Windows, but I'll show a way to reproduce by cloning, which was how I first encountered the issue.)

Environment: Windows 10, with output of `pip list` being
```
Package    Version
---------- ---------
certifi    2022.9.24
dulwich    0.20.50
pip        21.1.1
setuptools 56.0.0
urllib3    1.26.12
```

1. Create a new git repository that we're going to clone. In Powershell:

```
mkdir C:\source_repo
cd C:\source_repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m "Initial commit"
```

2. Try to clone it using dulwich:

```
python -c "from dulwich import porcelain; porcelain.clone('C:\\source_repo\\', 'C:\\cloned_repo')"
```

(note the trailing backslash in the path for `source_repo` -- without it it works fine).

**Expected result**

The `dulwich.porcelain.clone` command works and clones the repository.

**Actual result**

We get an exception:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\Users\hliu\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\config.py", line 413, in _parse_string
    v = _ESCAPE_TABLE[value[i]]
KeyError: 102

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\porcelain.py", line 551, in clone
    return client.clone(
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\client.py", line 761, in clone
    _import_remote_refs(
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\refs.py", line 1211, in _import_remote_refs
    refs_container.import_refs(
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\refs.py", line 187, in import_refs
    self.set_if_equals(
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\refs.py", line 871, in set_if_equals
    self._log(
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\refs.py", line 128, in _log
    self._logger(ref, old_sha, new_sha, committer, timestamp, timezone, message)
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\repo.py", line 1207, in _write_reflog
    config = self.get_config_stack()
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\repo.py", line 713, in get_config_stack
    backends = [self.get_config()] + StackedConfig.default_backends()
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\repo.py", line 1602, in get_config
    return ConfigFile.from_path(path)
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\config.py", line 593, in from_path
    ret = cls.from_file(f)
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\config.py", line 583, in from_file
    value = _parse_string(continuation)
  File "C:\Users\<username>\venvs\test_dulwich\lib\site-packages\dulwich\config.py", line 419, in _parse_string
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: escape character followed by unknown character 102 at 16 in bytearray(b'C:\\\\source_repo\\fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*')
```

**Analysis**

I believe this is a result of incorrect parsing of the git config file by dulwich.

When you clone the repository like this, the contents of `C:\cloned_repo\.git\config` will contain a section like:

```
[remote "origin"]
	url = C:\\source_repo\\
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*
```

dulwich (incorrectly) treats the final backslash in `url = C:\\source_repo\\` as a line continuation character, so joins the two lines, and then gives an error when trying to parse `url = C:\\source_repo\\fetch ...`

The code to do this is [here](https://github.com/jelmer/dulwich/blob/master/dulwich/config.py#L567-L580), where we simply treat every line ending in backslash as continuing onto the next line. This is incorrect in when the actual value on the line ends in an escape sequence `\\`.

Compare to how the git code parses config files [here](https://github.com/git/git/blob/c03801e19cb8ab36e9c0d17ff3d5e0c3b0f24193/config.c#L848-L849), which correctly parses the line one character at a time, and ends up treating the final backslash in `url = C:\\source_repo\\` as "consumed" as part of an escape sequence `\\`.

# Reproduce

0. Helm version v3.17.1+g980d8ac

1. Install any CRD

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: datas.crd.com
spec:
  group: crd.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: datas
    singular: data
    kind: Data
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
```

2. Apply a custom resource onto the cluster.

```yaml
kind: Data
apiVersion: crd.com/v1
metadata:
  name: crd-test
  namespace: kube-system
  labels:
    test: adopt
spec:
  color: blue
  size: large
```

3. `helm install --take-ownership` a chart that contains a different version of the custom resource.

```yaml
kind: Data
apiVersion: crd.com/v1
metadata:
  name: crd-test
  namespace: kube-system
  labels:
    test: adopt
spec:
  weight: heavy
```

4. Notice that the custom resource has not changed at all (still at initial state) but helm reported the operation to have succeeded, including the creation of a helm release.

```
helm install foo ./foo --take-ownership 
NAME: foo
LAST DEPLOYED: Wed Mar  5 17:10:16 2025
NAMESPACE: default
STATUS: deployed
REVISION: 1
TEST SUITE: None
```

# Suggested Solution

Transparently use three-way merge for `--take-ownership`.

Unable to upgrade packages which are circular peer dependencies
- [x] I have searched for [similar issues](https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/issues)
- [x] I am using the latest version of `npm-check-updates`
- [x] I am using `node >= 14.14`

---

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the following `package.json`, run `npm install` then `npm run test`.

```json
{
  "name": "npm-check-updates-circular-peer",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "npm-check-updates --peer"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@vitest/ui": "^1.3.1",
    "npm-check-updates": "^16.14.17",
    "vitest": "^1.3.1"
  }
}
```

The output will be the following:

```
Ignored incompatible updates (peer dependencies):

 @vitest/ui  ^1.3.1  →  ^1.4.0  reason: vitest requires 1.3.1
 vitest      ^1.3.1  →  ^1.4.0  reason: @vitest/ui requires 1.3.1
```

Both of these vitest packages depend on each other (eg: their versions must be kept in sync). This makes it impossible to update one without the other, both need to be updated together.

It'd be great if the peer dependency check could see if the version that it wants to update package A to would then no longer cause a conflict with package B.

It seems like currently what is happening is:

* Get the latest versions of each package
* Check if the latest version of a package conflicts with the current version of every other package

I'm suggesting:

* Get the latest versions of each package
* Check if the latest version of a package conflicts with the proposed (new) version of every other package

Feature Request: Check cmd state deprecation
### Preface
Kindly use the [check for state.cmd deprecation](https://github.com/roaldnefs/salt-lint/pull/37) as an example of adding a check. #37 has to be merged first.

### Description

Add the possibility to check for deprecation within the [cmd state](https://docs.saltstack.com/en/latest/ref/states/all/salt.states.cmd.html)

The following options have been deprecated:
* `cmd.run:quiet` (since _version 2014.1.0_)

The following options should be used:
* `cmd.run:output_loglevel: quiet`

Example(s) of an **improperly** configured state:
```code
getpip:
  cmd.run:
    - name: /usr/bin/python /usr/local/sbin/get-pip.py
    - unless: which pip
    - require:
      - pkg: python
      - file: /usr/local/sbin/get-pip.py
    - reload_modules: True
    - quiet
```

An example of **properly** configured state:
```code
getpip:
  cmd.run:
    - name: /usr/bin/python /usr/local/sbin/get-pip.py
    - unless: which pip
    - require:
      - pkg: python
      - file: /usr/local/sbin/get-pip.py
    - reload_modules: True
    - output_loglevel: quiet
```

### Fix requirements
A fix for this issue should (at least):
* Notify the user of using a deprecated option
* Notify the user since what version the option will be or has been deprecated
* A suggestion on what option to replace it with
* Contain unit tests for the check

Unable to queue EntrySaved listener when collection has no route
### Bug description

If you add the `ShouldQueue` trait to an `EntrySaved` listener and the entry being saved belongs to a collection with no route set you will get a `Serialization of 'Closure' is not allowed ` error when saving.

This happens because in `EntriesController` the entries `slug` property is set to a closure. If the collection has a route set the slug getter is called during `validateUniqueUri`/`entryUri` and that replaces the closure with its return value. But if the collection has no route set the getter is never called so the closure is left behind, causing a serialisation error when the job is queued.

### How to reproduce

1. Create a collection with no route set
2. Create an entry
3. Add an `EntrySaved` listener that implements `ShouldQueue`
4. Try to save the entry

Device service PUT Resource handling shall normally publish an update to the Message Bus
# 🚀 Feature Request

### Relevant Package [**REQUIRED**]
This feature request is a change for the device-sdk-go handling of the PUT /device/name/{device}/{command} API.
Later will extend to the device-sdk-c.

### Description [**REQUIRED**]
Core-command's GET /device/name/{device}/{command} has an optional query parameter, ds-pushevent, which is described as "If set to yes, a successful GET will result in an event being pushed to the EdgeX system". 
There is a desire for a similar capability for the matching PUT API, to notify other services of an update to the Resource(s), and to update core-data.


### Describe the solution you'd like
Change the Device SDK's PUT /device/name/{device}/{command} API handling, as normally sent by core-command,
to publish the updated Resource value(s) to the Message Bus as long as the Resource(s) are not write-only.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
The workaround today is to follow the PUT with a GET /device/name/{device}/{command} with ds-pushevent set to true, but this is just extra traffic to achieve the desired end.

The first draft of this Feature Request described adding a field to the data payload to indicate that the Resource value(s) should be published to the Message Bus. But, in discussion at the Architect's meeting, it was decided that we would almost always want to have the value published. The exception is for secrets or other write-only resources. So no need to require an additional field, and no worry that it might be omitted when it should be provided.

Add EmptyCriterion for easier generic queries
There are cases when you are building query complex criterion based on some external checks.
And in those cases you could want to have some empty criterion to build you complex criterion from it.

Basic case, where you have dict of argument and want to have any corresponding rows, could look like this:
```
criterion = EmptyCriterion()

for key, value in filters.items():
    criterion |= (table.key == value)

query = query.where(criterion)
```

Which right now would look like this:
```
criterion = None

for key, value in filters.items():
    if not criterion:
        criterion = (table.key == value)
    else:
        criterion |= (table.key == value)

if criterion:
    query = query.where(criterion) 
```

Also, there could be more complex cases where you got two criterions from some generic functions, and there you would have to do:
```
if not criterion1 and criterion2:
    res_criterion = criterion2
elif criterion1 and not criterion2:
    res_criterion = criterion1
else:
   res_criterion = criterion1 | criterion2
```
While, if functions could return EmptyCriterion, you could just do:
```
res_criterion = criterion1 | criterion2
```

Does this seem like good idea for you? If you approve this design I could try implementing it

Allow entity components enabling order on hierarchy change
When working with custom components (e.g. added via code), we need some components to be enabled before others. At the moment the components are called in random order:

https://github.com/playcanvas/engine/blob/55a3ff8845f0cf30829aeec515f24ac98b6baf4d/src/framework/entity.js#L503-L520

For example, a body component and a constraint component for physics. The constraint component needs a body to be attached to. If the body component is enabled later, it will be added to the physics after the constraint, which will fail creating the constraint as it will fail to locate the body.

There is no elegant way of doing it today. We have to introduce a component dependency into another component that actually doesn't need to be aware if other components and their state. We also have to add some sort of systems to queue up the creation commands to wait for the other component to be enabled, which is pretty brittle.

Add `spin up` option to mount static asset directory directly
Currently, `spin up` always copies static assets into a temporary directory and mounts that into the host.  This creates friction when iteratively developing static assets (e.g. SPAs) since `spin up` must be restarted each time any asset changes in order for the updated asset to be served.

I'm proposing that we add an option, e.g. `--direct-mount` to mount the asset directory directly instead of using a temporary directory, so that changes on the host filesystem are immediately visible to subsequent app invocations, with no restart required.

Add support for union types
A union type is a set consisting of multiple non-overlapping types. With union types, we can have function signatures of the type:

```elixir
fn foo : {:ok, Int} | {:error, String} do
  if true do
    {:ok, 123}
  else
    {:error, "Something went wrong"}
  end
end
```

We'll need to understand the concept of subtypes before we start working on this. [This wiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtyping) is a good introduction.

In this example:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1707078/95010225-33699680-0645-11eb-9064-032975e96198.png)
duck is a subtype of bird (which is its supertype), which means it can be substituted wherever a bird is expected. Similarly, a union type is a supertype of each member of the set.

Changes required:

1. Allow if-else branches to return different types. The inferred type of the if-else expression will be a union of the two types. This can be represented using a new "Union" struct that can be defined [here](https://github.com/fika-lang/fika/blob/master/lib/fika/types.ex) like the FunctionRef struct. The to_string function of the struct will join the types separated by " | ".
2. When [inferring the return type of a function](https://github.com/fika-lang/fika/blob/master/lib/fika/type_checker.ex#L52), we'll now expand union types and add all possible function types in [add_function_type](https://github.com/fika-lang/fika/blob/master/lib/fika/type_checker.ex#L402). Example:

```elixir
# A function that takes x which can be either :foo or :bar and returns either :ok or :error
fn foo(x: :foo | :bar) : :ok | :error do
  # ...
end
```

The type checker will add the following function types to its "function_types" map in env:
1. module.foo(:foo) => :ok 
2. module.foo(:foo) => :error
3. module.foo(:bar) => :ok
4. module.foo(:bar) => :error 

We can optimize the storing and checking of function types later, but this should do for now.

Please let me know if I've missed something here!
